title: Infinity for Unlimited — Every Cell Number + Text + Check

intelligence.essence: The unlimited cells had no number, so the check marks looked off — a cell with only a check is a cell with a hole in it. The fix: **the INFINITY SIGN (∞) is the number for unlimited** — in the number block itself, silver/white (black-and-silver), a unique glyph on its own, sized to match the digit tiles, so the checks line up. And the consistency law that goes with it: **EVERY cell carries number + text + check mark, all of them, all aligned the same way** — never just number+check, never just text+check; every check must actually show. The builder applied it 17:42Z: every unlimited cell carries a silver ∞ tile as its number, and every cell is number + text + check, aligned.
intelligence.human_view: Imagine a scoreboard where one column is blank because "unlimited" isn't a number — the checks beside it float, unanchored, and the whole board looks off. Give unlimited its own number: ∞, in its own tile, silver, the same size as the digits. Now every column has a number, every number has its words underneath, every cell has its check — and the board lines up, row after row, because nothing is missing anywhere.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a row of boxes, and one box is empty because someone said "this one is unlimited, so it doesn't need a number." The empty box makes the whole row look wrong. Put a special sign in it — ∞, the forever sign, in shiny silver, the same size as the other numbers. Now every box has a number, every number has words, every box has a tick — and they all line up perfectly.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, if a thing is unlimited, say so with a number of its own — the forever sign, ∞, in silver, sitting in its own little tile just like the other numbers. And every box on the board should hold the same three things: the number, the words that say what it is, and the tick that says you have it. All of them, all lined up the same way. Nothing half-empty, nothing missing.
intelligence.ai_view: I never leave a cell without a number — unlimited gets ∞, silver/white, a unique glyph on its own tile, sized to match the digit tiles, so the checks line up. I never ship a cell with two of the three: every cell carries number + text + check, all aligned the same way, and every check actually shows. A missing number is a hole the eye falls into; a missing check is a promise the board doesn't keep. The board is only true when every cell is complete.
intelligence.what_it_means:
1. **∞ is the number for unlimited.** In the number block itself, silver/white (black-and-silver), a unique glyph on its own, sized to match the digit tiles.
2. **The checks line up because the numbers line up.** An unlimited cell without a number throws the whole column off.
3. **Consistency law: every cell, number + text + check.** All of them, all aligned the same way — never just number+check, never just text+check.
4. **Every check must actually show.** A check that doesn't render is a cell that lies about what the level includes.
5. **Done 17:42Z:** silver ∞ tile in every unlimited cell; every cell number + text + check, aligned. Presented to Shawn; his eye decides.
